claims.text: The three frozen source Questions ask how RabbitMQ/MQ prevents message loss, including an explicit consumer-side variant, so the answer must cover publisher, broker and consumer failure boundaries rather than only one mechanism.

Publisher confirms provide publisher-to-broker acceptance feedback; unconfirmed messages can be retransmitted after failures, and mandatory/basic.return is a separate routing-failure signal when the application requires a routed destination.

Durable queues plus persistent publication semantics address restart recovery, while quorum queues add replicated data-safety semantics whose confirm boundary is tied to quorum acceptance and majority availability assumptions.

Manual consumer acknowledgement after the intended business-success boundary enables redelivery of unacknowledged deliveries on failure; nack/reject controls requeue versus discard/dead-letter policy.

Retransmission and redelivery can create duplicates, so loss prevention must be paired with idempotent or deduplicated business effects and must not be described as RabbitMQ-provided end-to-end exactly-once processing.
